title: Stress-Testing Practices and Scenario Design

maps.tested: Described as 'a full important chapter - stress testing has always been a favourite topic of GARP.' A recall independently reports 2-3 questions.
maps.specifics: Reported: '2-3 questions on stress testing related - appropriate practices', i.e. best-practice audits rather than computation. Market-driven scenarios (Reading 97) supply the plausible-scenario-construction angle. The SCAP / EBA / CCAR sibling swap on which regime required what, and which banks failed, is the historical-fact layer.

vardeezReading: CR-21: Very Important. "Full Important Chapter. Stress Testing has always been favorite topic of Garp." ORR-17: Important, no note. IM-15: Very Important. "Mahalanobis Distance, Scenario, Volatility and Correlation Z-Scores (remember Learning Objective is EXPLAIN - so no need to get hung up on Formulas), Market-Driven Scenario Construction (know how to create it)."

los.vardeez: Mahalanobis distance, scenario / volatility / correlation z-scores. LO verb is EXPLAIN: no need to get hung up on formulas
Know how to construct a market-driven scenario

selectors.name: Appropriate stress-testing practices audit
selectors.what: Best-practice audit of a stress-testing programme rather than a computation: what to stress, how to aggregate the results, and what to avoid (the common pitfalls of CCR stress tests, and the challenges of scenario design and coherence).

selectors.name: Market-driven scenario construction and z-scores
selectors.what: Plausible scenario construction by the market-driven approach: the steps, the choice of few policy variables, the covariance choice, and the scenario, volatility and correlation z-scores and Mahalanobis distance as measures of severity and plausibility.

selectors.name: SCAP, EBA, CCAR sibling swap
selectors.what: Which supervisory regime (SCAP, CEBS, EBA, CCAR) did or required what: scenario features, post-stress capital hurdles, disclosure, risk weights used, and which banks failed or raised capital.

selectors.name: Pre-SCAP versus post-SCAP stress testing
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Pre-SCAP vs post-SCAP' on ORR-17 a
selectors.what: How supervisory stress testing changed with SCAP: why supervisors stress test banks (adequately capitalised by regulatory rules before failing), the credible capital-hole estimate and backstop, and bank-level disclosure of projected losses.

notSelected: CR-21 a to g (exposure measures, CCR as credit and as market risk, the loan, derivative, CVA and DVA stress calculations) carry no pinned shape and are covered only as the practices and pitfalls of S1, ORR-17 c (modelling losses, revenues and the balance sheet) and IM-15 d (implementation challenges) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer, and the Mahalanobis distance formula is not selected because the Vardeez pointer says not to get hung up on formulas.
